title: Luxury Rental Fraud: How Identity Verification Protects Designer Bags and Watches
summary: Learn how luxury rental fraud affects designer bag and watch businesses, and how identity verification helps prevent fraud and protect valuable inventory.
body_markdown:
Luxury rental businesses allow customers to borrow high-value items, such as designer handbags and luxury watches, without requiring them to pay the full retail price. However, the value and portability of these items can make them attractive targets for fraud, including identity theft, payment fraud, and rentals made with the intention of keeping or reselling items illegally.


**Luxury rental fraud prevention** involves more than collecting a photo ID or payment details. Businesses need reliable ways to verify renters’ identities, identify inconsistencies, and assess potential risks before handing over valuable items. By integrating identity verification into the rental process, platforms can reduce exposure to fraud while providing a more secure experience for legitimate customers.


## **Why Are Luxury Rentals a Growing Fraud Target?**


Designer handbags, luxury watches, and other high-value accessories are common targets for fraud because they are portable, expensive, and relatively easy to resell. This creates risks for rental businesses when customers use stolen identities, fraudulent payment details, or misleading information to obtain items they may never intend to return. **Luxury rental fraud** can result in lost inventory, replacement costs, and reduced customer trust.


The risk is usually more difficult to manage when businesses depend on basic identity checks that cannot verify whether the person making a booking is the legitimate account holder. Fraudsters may use falsified documents, stolen personal information, or synthetic identities to get through registration. For luxury rental platforms, effective identity verification helps confirm who is renting an item and identify inconsistencies before valuable items are handed over.


## What Can Luxury Rental Fraud Cost Businesses?


Luxury rental fraud can lead to missing inventory, replacement costs, payment disputes, lost revenue, and reduced customer confidence. When expensive products such as designer handbags and luxury watches are involved, even a single incident can result in significant financial losses.[In early 2024, Japan’s Toke Match watch-sharing service](https://www.afpbb.com/articles/-/3508795) abruptly ceased operations, leaving hundreds of watch owners without their property. Approximately **900 luxury watches worth 1.9 billion yen (about US$12.6 million at the time)** remained unreturned, with some later found listed for resale. Although Toke Match operated a watch-sharing service rather than a conventional luxury rental platform, the case illustrates the potential financial impact when high-value items entrusted to a business are not returned. It also shows how missing inventory can undermine confidence in businesses built around access to luxury goods.


Fraud is also a recognised business risk in the wider apparel rental industry. In its[2026 annual report filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1468327/000146832726000088/rent-20260731.htm) , Rent the Runway disclosed that it had incurred, and could continue to incur, losses from various forms of fraud. These included purchases made with stolen credit cards, customers fraudulently renting multiple products at once, and customers failing to return rentals. The disclosure highlights the financial risks fraud poses to rental businesses and the importance of identifying suspicious bookings before valuable items are released.


These examples highlight how fraud and inventory losses can affect rental and luxury-sharing businesses, leading to financial setbacks and reduced customer confidence. Implementing reliable identity verification, payment checks, and reviews of suspicious bookings can help businesses identify potential risks before handing over valuable items.


## **How Does Identity Verification Help Prevent Luxury Rental Fraud?**


Identity verification helps luxury rental businesses establish that the person booking an item is the same person collecting the item. Relying on a photo ID alone can leave gaps if someone uses a stolen, borrowed, or altered document. For businesses renting out high-value items, more robust identity checks can reduce the risk of fraudulent rentals, unauthorised collections, and losses involving designer handbags or luxury watches.


Effective **identity verification for rental businesses** combines several checks rather than relying on just one. Businesses can check submitted identity documents, compare personal details for inconsistencies, and use biometric facial matching where available to assess whether the renter matches the photograph on their ID. These checks help identify potential risks before an item is handed over, while allowing staff to investigate suspicious cases instead of relying solely on a visual document check.
